correctness.rationale: Schoenberg reduces the cone to nonnegative summable coefficients of the normalized Gegenbauer kernels; the Bernstein operator is continuous in sup norm, so checking all basis kernels suffices. For the top coefficient, the exponential response of the signed centered n-difference is (2sinh(z/n))^n. Its first two even-spaced nonzero powers give D_n(t^n)=n!(2/n)^n and D_n(t^(n+2))/D_n(t^n)=(n+1)(n+2)/(6n). The two top normalized Gegenbauer coefficients contribute L_(n+2) times the difference of this ratio and (n+1)(n+2)/[4(n+λ+1)]. Dividing the top monomial coefficient by L_n, using L_m=2^m(λ)_m/(2λ)_m, gives the published-in-record formula and sign d+1−n. At d=2, n=4 it is −9/256; at n=d+1 the zero coefficient gives no positivity conclusion in higher dimensions. For n=1,2,3 I verified the parity reductions and all low-degree coefficient formulas; for n=3 odd the P_3 coefficient is (1−3P_m(1/3))/10. Laplace's integral gives |P_m|≤1 and for m≥9 at 1/3 an upper bound by the fourth moment of 1−(8/9)sin²u, namely 1921/6561<1/3. The exact m=1,3,5,7 evaluations fill in every smaller odd degree. Thus the iff on S² and the necessary higher-dimensional bound hold with the stated dot-product nodes and normalization.
residual_risks: The arithmetic replay is finite; the generating identity and integral estimate prove the universal claims. Sufficiency for d>2 is not part of the frozen finding.
